title: Config change rollback oracle and stability harmonizer
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Background: As we push automatic batching and prefix/KV cache recommendations into runtime, small config changes have increasingly complex downstream effects on latency distributions and per-token cost. Previously we relied on simple canary percentages and metric thresholds for rollbacks. This ticket builds an automated ‘oracle’ that evaluates risk, stages safe applies, and harmonizes live state when a revert is required.

Goals: 1) Provide an autonomous decision layer (oracle) that can: a) simulate the expected cost/latency delta for a config change using historical traffic slices, b) mark changes as safe/conditional/high-risk, and c) recommend a staging plan (shadow/apply/canary ramp) for operators. 2) Implement a state harmonizer that can reconcile KV cache and batching state after an applied change or automatic revert without user-visible correctness regressions. 3) Add guardrails / tripwires for automatic safe reversion on SLO regressions, cost spikes, or cache corruption signals. 4) Integrate with Console rollouts so PMs and SREs can opt-in/out and view the oracle’s reasoning.

Nonfunctional requirements: - Reversion path must complete within defined SLO: 30s median, 95th 2m. - The oracle must maintain false-positive revert rate < 2% on historical replay tests. - Any automatic revert must produce a complete event + snapshot for incident review. - No changes should cause user-level correctness regressions (structured output failures) more than once per 10k requests during canary.

Architecture overview: - Simulation engine: replays representative traffic windows against candidate config patches in a sandbox (prefix/KV cache emulator + batching scheduler) to estimate token cost delta and tail latency. - Risk scorer: combines simulation results with historic variance, model skew, and dependency signals (GPU kernel fallbacks, quantization flags) to produce a risk tier. - Apply orchestrator: stages changes using a multi-stage plan (shadow apply -> 1% canary -> 5% -> 25% -> 100%) with customizable hysteresis and hold windows. - Tripwire layer: configured metric checks (latency_95, token_cost_per_minute, error_rate, cache_mismatch_rate) that can trigger immediate pause or revert. - State harmonizer: coordinated snapshot & replay mechanism that checkpoints KV cache shards, tags streaming connections, and ensures safe warming after revert or apply. - Audit & explainability: every decision stored as immutable event with simulation artifacts, diff links, and a human-readable rationale to surface in Console.

Acceptance criteria: - Oracle simulation engine runs end-to-end on nightly replay job and produces risk classification within SLA. - Orchestrator can execute a staged apply plan with manual hold and auto-continue. - Tripwire-based automatic revert completes and restores previous state in <= 2 minutes for 95% of test scenarios. - Console shows the oracle’s decision, the simulation summary, and links to the revert playbook. - Unit/integration tests cover cache checkpoint/replay, canary ramping, and revert decision logic.

Open questions / tradeoffs: - How conservative should the oracle be for cost-optimization changes vs reliability? Default suggestion: bias toward safety for first two weeks after initial rollout, then allow more aggressive cost optimizations. - Do we allow automatic revert for customer-visible semantic drift (structured output)? Proposal: require human approval for semantic regressions detected by eval sets, but allow automatic revert for infra-level regressions (latency/cost/availability). - Snapshot size and frequency for KV cache checkpoints vs performance overhead. Current plan: incremental diffs every 30s during canary windows.

Implementation plan (high level): 1. Prototype simulation engine and scoring (week 1-2). 2. Implement apply orchestrator with canary ramps and tripwire hooks (week 3-4). 3. Build state harmonizer with checkpointing and replay glue (week 4-6). 4. Integrate with Console and add audit trail (week 5-7). 5. End-to-end replay tests, chaos injection, and security review (week 7-8). 6. Gradual rollout and postmortem process.

T2: Define risk scoring model and thresholds (collab with Applied ML)
T3: Implement orchestrator API + canary ramp engine
T4: Add metric tripwire hooks and alerting integration
T5: Design and implement KV cache checkpoint/replay protocol
T6: Console UI: decision explainer and opt controls
T7: Add e2e tests and nightly replay job
T8: Run security and compliance review

acceptance_tests: AT1: Replay job produces risk classification for 5 historical windows and matches manual labels >= 95% of time
AT2: Canary apply and automatic revert flow restores previous runtime state and KV caches with no structured-output errors in test corpus
AT3: Revert event and simulation artifacts are present in audit trail and Console within 30s of decision
AT4: Performance overhead of checkpointing during canary < 5% CPU and < 3% latency increase
